title: StratumTracker network replay high-water LRU is eviction-exposed to DIOs never authorized for time (replay-window bypass)
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-fxrh. python/src/lichen/timing/stratum.py:629-632 inserts and move_to_end-refreshes the (signer,generation)->counter barrier UNCONDITIONALLY once the counter is new, BEFORE the time-authorization and payload-binding checks that run later inside _rejection via _adopt_claimed_locked (network-transport-not-authorized / network-peer-not-authorized-for-time at stratum.py:185-188, network-option-evidence-mismatch at 193-197). Rejected, unauthorized-for-time DIOs therefore consume and order LRU slots. Same-signer eviction (626-628) caps each signer at one entry, but with MAX_NETWORK_REPLAY_GENERATIONS=256 (time_sync.py:58) an attacker controlling >=256 distinct signer keys admitted to the verifier's peer_origins can flood the OrderedDict and evict a victim signer's high-water entry; __network_high_water.get(replay_key,-1) at 623 then returns -1 and ANY counter passes: a previously-considered validly-signed victim DIO re-verified into a fresh sample is considered again. With no current sample the stale sample skips backward-step (690-691) and stratum/precedence (680-685) checks, so a sufficiently old floor-passing timestamp can adopt = time rollback. Preconditions (256+ keys in peer_origins, LRU race vs the victim's refresh, low epoch floor) are deployment-dependent but plausible under open mesh admission. Fix directions: only insert/refresh LRU entries for samples whose authority is authorized for time (move the barrier insert after _rejection's authorization checks, or gate on the authorization verdict before 629); or track victim eviction via a tombstone floor that survives eviction; or size-bound per-signer with a persistent floor file like the announce/gateway stores. Also consider whether issuance_high_water (609-612, no eviction) already bounds the same reissue path and document the interplay.
